title:
Comment of Betsy Peratrovich in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15423-000
Submission Date: 11/2/2026

documents.name: 152218.txt
documents.text:
Betsy Peratrovich, Anchorage, AK.
This submission represents my formal request—as an Alaska Native citizen residing in the Cook Inlet region of Alaska—for the Commission to deny the preliminary permit application filed by DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC for the proposed underwater hyperscale data center and tidal energy project in Cook Inlet, Alaska (Docket No. P-15423-000). 

The proposed project presents profound, unstudied and irreversible risks to the marine ecosystem, endangered species and commercial and subsistence fisheries.

The project scale would span an unprecedented 1,650 acres of subsea land, positioning up to 350 tidal turbines and 66 data center hives in a highly dynamic and ecologically sensitive environment. 

This presents several critical issues:

* The proposed project sits directly within critical habitat for the Cook Inlet beluga whale, an endangered population currently numbering fewer than 300 individuals. The continuous underwater acoustic noise and vibrations generated by hundreds of rotating turbines and data center cooling systems could severely disrupt beluga echolocation, masking communication and driving them away from their vital feeding and calving grounds.

* The Forelands region acts as a natural geographical bottleneck in Cook Inlet, and serves as a primary migratory corridor for all five species of wild Alaskan salmon returning to the Kenai and Susitna river systems. Placing a massive array of marine hydrokinetic turbines in this narrow corridor creates a severe risk of fish strikes, blade injury and mortality, for both adult salmon and out-migrating smolt.

* Hyperscale data centers generate immense thermal energy, and discharging waste heat directly into the subsea environment risks creating localized thermal plumes. These temperature shifts can disrupt the delicate environmental signals that wild salmon rely on for migration, and alter the local marine food web.

* The project—proposed as an "off-grid" facility dedicated solely to external data processing—offers zero benefit, energy security or grid stabilization to Kenai Peninsula communities. In addition, the developer has failed to engage in transparent, robust public outreach with local stakeholders, including community members and Alaska Native tribes who rely heavily on these waters.

Given that underwater data centers powered by massive tidal arrays are an unproven technology at this scale, the potential for catastrophic ecological failure is simply too high. FERC must prioritize the long-term health of Cook Inlet’s waters, wildlife, and coastal economies over private, experimental industrial development.

Thank you for your time, consideration.
